name: Workflow Acceleration Toolkit
description: Led the development of a plugin suite, cutting down company's production time by 60%

items.label: Faster design system setup and configuration
Saved engineering costs through reduced handoff iterations

pain.headline: Understanding why mid-budget contracts were taking too long to produce
body: The company needed a way to shrink production time, without adding headcount or slowing down quality.
I sat down with Design, Sales, Development, and PM to find out. Four recurring pain points came up:
list: Design System colors and typography needed constant manual adjustment
Navigating prototypes during client presentations was clunky
Exporting tokens to development had no clear process
Pulling copy from mockups for the client copywriting doc was fully manual

source.headline: Every pain point traced back to the same file: Figma
body: Four different problems, one shared source. Figma's plugin system was the obvious lever. The real question was how to structure it.

split.headline: I split the fix into three plugins, one per workflow
body: Bundling everything into a single tool would have dumped all the work on designers. Instead, I segmented by need and audience:
list: Style Studio: token & style management for Design
Site Mapper: prototype navigation for Design, Sales, and PM
Text 2 Sheet: copy extraction for PM

tokens.headline: What do designers and developers actually need from tokens?
body: I worked directly with the design team to define core features, then partnered with staff engineers to align token exports with their pipeline. Benchmarking existing design systems and plugins helped the features coexist in one coherent interface.

prototype.headline: Consultants didn't want to follow the prototype flow
body: They wanted to jump straight to a specific page, or see only a limited subset of the prototype, not the full click-through. The fix was pretty obvious: auto-generate a sitemap so any exposed page is one click away.

copy.headline: Managers required a specific copywriting output
body: The text extractor tool was part of a broader automation system, as a result I worked closely with my manager to shape the CSV output for a downstream internal tool.

layout.headline: One layout didn't fit every element
body: Colors worked well shown as swatches, but fonts displayed the same way (i.e. plain boxes), weren't legible enough to adjust with confidence. Switching to a full detail list (real size, letter spacing) fixed that, but made the list cumbersome to browse in the plugin's small window.
I added two extra layout options for colors and fonts, balancing quick scanning with precise editing. The team's feedback on the new layouts was positive.

tagging.headline: Tagging text one layer at a time didn't scale, I proposed a faster flow
body: Text2Sheet's first flow required selecting and marking text layers individually, too slow for real projects. I used the Figma API to auto-extract every text layer on a selected frame at once, adding filters to keep the output manageable. My manager's feedback on the change was positive as it greatly reduced the workload.

latency.headline: The first-load latency for bigger project needed to be fixed
body: The plugin ran fine on small files, but slowed to a crawl past 10+ pages. I rebuilt the storage layer to store only node IDs and load each tab's data asynchronously, instead of loading everything upfront. Initial load time dropped from 12 seconds to 89 milliseconds.

phasing.headline: Each plugin shipped in phases, timed to departments urgency
body: As I was the sole developer for this project, features were sequenced across Q1 to Q4 rather than shipped all at once, keeping scope realistic per team.

adoption.headline: A tool nobody understands doesn't get adopted
body: I wrote a cross-department source-of-truth doc covering not just the plugins, but Figma best practices in general: comment conventions, client prototype sharing, and more. Live training sessions with each department closed the gap written docs couldn't.

results.headline: The toolkit reached 2,000+ users
body: It accelerated Design System adjustments from 1 hour to 20 minutes, made handoff faster by reducing by half the loopback between designer and developers, and community feedback kept improving it after launch like including Figma's sections in the navigation map or supporting manual variables reload.

list.title: Less over-engineering.
list.body: Style Studio used Redux with async thunks for a simple state management, more complexity than the plugin needed. I now default to the simplest state model that works and scale up only when the data proves it's necessary.

list.title: Giving a greater attention to the adoption strategy.
list.body: Style Studio's token workflow still needs hand-holding for junior designers less familiar with design systems. I set in-app guidance (tips, hints, onboarding) and documentation as next phase priority.

list.title: Rethinking the pipeline rather than a part of it.
list.body: Text2Sheet fixed extraction, but it still sits inside a multi-tool export chain, which is why some PMs skip it entirely. The next iteration would aim to centralize the export process into one tool.
